concepts.name: Confining ions
concepts.statement: Ions respond strongly to applied electric fields through the Coulomb force, which allows extremely tight traps, but one cannot create a static electric field minimum, so an ion cannot be confined by static electric fields alone; magnetic fields or RF electric fields provide the 3D confinement.

concepts.name: Penning trap
concepts.statement: The Penning trap confines the ion in two dimensions by its cyclotron motion in a magnetic field and in the third by charged endcaps; the crossed electric and magnetic fields add a larger-scale magnetron motion.

concepts.name: Quadrupole potential
concepts.statement: A quadrupole electric potential whose coefficients sum to zero by Laplace's equation, so that with α = −β, γ = 0 it confines in one direction and repels in the other.

concepts.name: Paul trap
concepts.statement: The Paul trap simulates an electric field minimum with a high-frequency quadrupole potential: averaged over many cycles of the oscillating saddle, the net effect is to confine the ion, in three dimensions with charged endcaps added.

concepts.name: Micromotion
concepts.statement: The ion follows the motion of the oscillating trap, 180 degrees out of phase with it, so it meets the repulsive potential near the centre and the confining one far from it.

concepts.name: Trapped-ion model
concepts.statement: For our purposes an ion trap can be approximated by a harmonic oscillator potential, the ion subject to laser excitation and spontaneous emission.

concepts.name: Cooling and qubit transitions
concepts.statement: A dipole allowed transition relaxes quickly and is used for laser cooling and for readout by fluorescence; a long-lived metastable state driven on a quadrupole transition, with lifetime around a second, is used for encoding information.

concepts.name: Internal and motional states
concepts.statement: The Hilbert space of the trapped ion is a two level system together with a harmonic oscillator ladder of Fock states describing its quantized motion.

concepts.name: Ion position and momentum operators
concepts.statement: The ion's position and momentum are written with the creation and annihilation operators of a quantum of vibrational energy in a trap of frequency ν.

concepts.name: Trap frequency
concepts.statement: The harmonic oscillator frequency ν of the trap, around 10 MHz for ions thanks to the strong Coulomb interaction.

concepts.name: Motional Hamiltonian
concepts.statement: The Hamiltonian of the ion's motion counts its vibrational quanta, each of energy ℏν.

concepts.name: Harmonic oscillator length
concepts.statement: The characteristic size of the ion's motional ground-state wave function, for tightly trapped ions significantly smaller than optical wavelengths.

concepts.name: Electronic Hamiltonian
concepts.statement: With spontaneous emission neglected, the ion's internal levels are a two-level system with ground state |g⟩ and excited state |e⟩ at ℏω_eg.

concepts.name: Negligible decay
concepts.statement: To neglect decay the rate γ must be small compared with the inverse of the manipulation time τ; this is reached with a metastable state driven on a quadrupole transition or with a far-detuned Raman transition, which reduces the effective linewidth by (Ω/∆)².

concepts.name: Ion-laser interaction
concepts.statement: The laser field acts at the ion's position, so x becomes the operator x̂ in the interaction Hamiltonian, for a running wave or a standing wave.

concepts.name: Momentum kick
concepts.statement: Absorbing a photon gives the ion a momentum kick ℏk, which can excite higher vibrational states, so laser excitation manipulates the centre of mass motion.

concepts.name: Lamb-Dicke parameter
concepts.statement: The ratio of the ion's spatial extent to the laser wavelength, a small parameter for tight traps; it is also the square root of the recoil frequency over the trap frequency.

concepts.name: Lamb-Dicke regime
concepts.statement: The limit in which the ion is so tightly bound that a photon's recoil energy cannot excite a higher vibrational state, so the photon momentum is absorbed by the trap rather than the ion; the real expansion parameter is η√n.

concepts.name: Trapped-ion Hamiltonian
concepts.statement: In the rotating frame the trapped ion's total Hamiltonian is the motion, the detuned internal level and the laser coupling, with η in the exponent for a running wave or in the sine for a standing wave.

concepts.name: Bare ion spectrum
concepts.statement: The bare states |g⟩|n⟩ and |e⟩|n⟩ are the ground and excited electronic levels, well separated since ω_eg ≫ ν, each subdivided into motional states spaced by ν.

concepts.name: Carrier and sideband couplings
concepts.statement: To lowest order in η a running wave couples |g⟩|n⟩ only to |e⟩|n⟩ with strength Ω and to |e⟩|n±1⟩ with strengths ηΩ√(n+1) and ηΩ√n; the three transitions are addressed individually by tuning the laser, and the sideband Rabi frequency grows with the phonon number.

concepts.name: Bare-resonance transition
concepts.statement: With the laser on the bare atomic resonance and weak enough, Ω ≪ ν/η, the sidebands are suppressed and the internal and motional degrees of freedom decouple: the ion cycles between internal states without changing its motional state.

concepts.name: Red sideband as Jaynes-Cummings model
concepts.statement: On the red sideband the ion obeys a Jaynes-Cummings model, internal transitions accompanied by creation or annihilation of a phonon, with the vacuum Rabi coupling replaced by g → ηΩ.

concepts.name: Strong coupling with ions
concepts.statement: Since the coupling ηΩ grows with laser power, the strong coupling regime is significantly easier to attain with ion traps than in cavity QED, and the coupling can be switched on and off with the laser.

concepts.name: Anti-Jaynes-Cummings model
concepts.statement: On the blue sideband the ion obeys an anti-Jaynes Cummings Hamiltonian, internal excitation accompanied by emission of a phonon and vice versa.

concepts.name: Standing-wave couplings
concepts.statement: In a standing wave the phase φ of the wave relative to the trap minimum is a further control: at φ = 0 the vertical transitions are eliminated and only the sidebands remain.

concepts.name: Sideband cooling
concepts.statement: A laser on the red sideband of an allowed transition lowers the motional energy in every excitation cycle while emission goes into all three transitions, pumping the ion on average into the trap ground state, which is dark to the laser.

concepts.name: Resolved sidebands
concepts.statement: The cooling rate is set by the fluorescence rate γ, but cooling into the ground state requires γ ≪ ν so that off-resonant excitation of the direct and blue sideband transitions can be neglected; a second laser coupling the forbidden level to an allowed one tunes the effective emission rate.

concepts.name: Arbitrary motional state
concepts.statement: An arbitrary motional state of the ion, with coefficients c_n that could be a Fock, coherent, squeezed or Schrodinger cat state; engineering such states is crucial to quantum gates in an ion trap.

concepts.name: Pulse sequence
concepts.statement: Laser pulses on the bare and sideband transitions are a series of unitary transformations linking an initial state to a final one.

concepts.name: Swap onto the motion
concepts.statement: A π pulse on the red sideband swaps information from the internal state onto the motional state.

concepts.name: Preparing a motional state
concepts.statement: Working backwards from the target state, alternate red-sideband and bare-resonance pulses empty the highest rung of the oscillator into the next until all the population is in the ground state; the inverse sequence prepares the state.

concepts.name: Ion string
concepts.statement: Ions in one anisotropic trap repel each other into a string spaced by 5-10 μm, far enough for a focussed laser to resolve each, while the Coulomb interaction couples their motion into phonon modes of different frequencies and spatial forms.

concepts.name: Two ions in a trap
concepts.statement: Two ions feel the harmonic confinement and their Coulomb repulsion, which to lowest order in their displacements from equilibrium adds a spring between them.

concepts.name: Centre-of-mass and stretch modes
concepts.statement: The two ions vibrate in a centre-of-mass mode at frequency ν and a stretch mode at √3ν, the symmetric and antisymmetric combinations of their displacements.

concepts.name: Two-ion Hamiltonian
concepts.statement: Each ion's laser couples its internal state to both phonon modes, with its own Lamb-Dicke parameter per mode, and the two modes can be separately addressed by choosing the laser detuning.

concepts.name: Qubit
concepts.statement: A two-level quantum system storing information, its internal states read as bit values |g⟩ = |0⟩ and |e⟩ = |1⟩ and the information encoded in the state α|0⟩ + β|1⟩.

concepts.name: Universal computation
concepts.statement: If each qubit can be addressed and rotated arbitrarily, universal computation needs only one non-trivial gate coupling any two-qubit pair.

concepts.name: π phase gate
concepts.statement: The two-qubit gate that flips the sign of one qubit's excited state only if the other qubit is also excited.

concepts.name: Phase gate requirements
concepts.statement: The trapped-ion phase gate needs the vibrational modes cooled to the ground state and an auxiliary level degenerate with the excited state, coupled to the ground state by an orthogonal laser polarization.

concepts.name: Ion-trap phase gate
concepts.statement: A phase gate between ions m and n writes qubit m onto the collective motion with a red-sideband π pulse, applies a 2π pulse to the auxiliary level of ion n conditional on the motion, and writes the motion back onto qubit m, leaving the state unchanged unless both qubits were excited, when it changes sign.
